questions.answer: I had to register for all my classes again. Something that I had already done so many times that I lost count.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The ESN network was always helpful and my coordinator from my home university could answer mails as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It will work in the end, but be ready to upload a million documents time and time again

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some classes were great, others downright bad

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them were the hardest classes I have yet to take. Others had a level comparable to 1g in our country.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I like the style at UCPH a lot more. Every professor had their own style and criteria here and it was very confusing. I also don't like the amount of classes, it is a lot and they happen at honestly weird times of the day.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fundamentos de lingüística general
Usos especializados del Español
Literatura y genero
Políticas de Interculturalidad en los países de habla inglesa
Historía del mundo actual

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Both of the english courses(the last two on my list) were very easy to me, but didn't provide a lot academically, if you're looking to be challenged.
Lit. y genero was good and interesting.
Fundamentos was a bit boring at times, but had the most interesting subject to me academically.
Usos was bad. Do not take this course. For some reason you have to create "class" where you teach one of the specialized languages. This would be fine, except you have to rigorously go through the standard spanish didactic practices. It is so in depth and so irrelevant to the rest of the course. I am not studying education, I am studying language. I like didactics, but that is not what the course is advertising itself as. Incredibly stressful for no reason.

questions.answer: ESN there is great and have won numerous awards because of this

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Again their ESN did many cultural and social activities and there were tournaments in different sports, but none that I was interested in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ESN network and going to different cities in Andalucía

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Granada is amazing and if you have the money try to take a trip to Morocco during the holidays

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was hard at first, but became easier as time went on

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the ESN activities. As a danish excange student you might feel a little lonely in the beginning because everyone else already know many people from their countries, but just throw yourself into it and be as brave as you can. The actual local spanish students can be a bit more standoffish so try to talk to them in your classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of late-ness. Most of the time the professors don't even arrive on time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Tapas. You will know when you get there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't take Usos.
Go to the ESN activities.
Make sure your room has either a fan or aircon for the summer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be intimidated by the thick accent. It is hard for everyone to understand, don't worry.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connections

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language. The accent is very thick and the big amount of classes and activities did not leave a lot of room for extra language classes.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
